decisions.executionNote: Approach the near upright white bottle with the left hand, opening maintained. Small initial increments to preserve the elbow branch; grasp offset estimated from RGB.
Replan from measured pose after continuity guard. Smaller advance and lowering toward the white bottle body.
Finish the small body-level approach and close the left gripper around the aligned white bottle; retention still needs a lift check.
Lift the white bottle and carry it left toward the bin, keeping the grasp closed. Verify retention in the next image before releasing.
White bottle visibly retained. Carry farther over the bin opening with the left hand closed, maintaining height and branch continuity.
Open over the bin to release the retained white bottle, then begin returning toward the standing blue bottle without crossing workspaces.
Move the open left gripper toward the blue standing bottle at body height, correcting yaw and approach tilt; inspect alignment before closing.
Lower slightly onto the blue bottle body, close fully, and start a small retention-check lift.
Blue bottle appears between the closed fingers. Lift clear and transport left toward the dustbin; keep closed until safely over the opening.
Blue bottle remained on the table, so the previous grip did not retain it. Reopen and return for a deeper, lower body grasp; next lift will be vertical before transport.
The blue bottle has tipped onto its side. Lift the open hand and progressively turn to a downward approach for a transverse body grasp, keeping the elbow configuration continuous.
No motion executed after the IK guard. Use half-sized lift and rotation increments from the measured pose to begin the overhead approach safely.
Continue raising and pitching the open hand toward an overhead grasp on the lying blue bottle; preserve the accepted elbow-up branch.
Align the overhead fingers across the lying blue bottle, moving slightly left and descending while completing the approach pitch. Keep open pending visual alignment.
Descend the last few millimeters around the blue bottle body and close fully. Hold position before a vertical retention check.
Lift vertically with the blue bottle grasp closed; use RGB displacement and finger contact to verify retention before transporting.
The bottle stayed on the table. Reopen and correct the overhead grasp to its new center; make the approach vertical to avoid lateral pushing.
After the continuity stop, keep the accepted orientation and use millimeter corrections to center the fingers over the blue bottle before closing.
Allow full closure at the aligned body, then make a very small vertical lift to check whether the bottle follows before transport.
The bottle did not follow and the wrist view shows a lateral miss. Reopen and shift the hand left to align its actual pinch point, with a small depth correction.
The bottle is now centered in the wrist view. Advance the overhead pinch slightly along its body, lower a little, and close without lifting yet.
Fingers visibly surround the blue bottle now. Finish closure and gently lift while easing back to avoid the tight folded reach; verify that the bottle moves with the hand.
The fingers closed above the bottle rather than retaining it. Reopen and lower the actual pinch point farther around the body, with only a small forward adjustment.
Lower another small amount around the centered bottle body, then hold still with full closure to establish contact before lifting.
Complete closure at the deeper grasp, then lift slowly while easing the elbow configuration; inspect whether the blue bottle follows.
The blue bottle now follows the lift and remains between the fingers. Carry upward and left toward the bin with the gripper closed, easing out of the overhead configuration.
Blue bottle visibly retained and clear of the table. Bring it over the bin opening, keeping closed and gradually relaxing the wrist pitch.
Center the held blue bottle farther over the bin and open the left gripper to release it. Hold the release position for visual confirmation.
Wait for the blue bottle to fall clear, then move the open left hand toward the remaining white bottle while beginning a gradual overhead grasp reorientation.
Two bottles are visible in the bin. Move toward the lying white bottle, rotating gradually so the fingers close across its axis; stay in the left workspace.
Continue above the white bottle and turn the pinch direction across its long axis, with clearance for the final descent.
Center the overhead pinch on the white bottle and descend to body level, using the deeper grasp height that retained the blue bottle.
Make a small lateral pinch-center correction from the wrist image, lower the last few millimeters, then close and hold on the white bottle.
Hold full closure briefly, then lift the white bottle gently and inspect its motion relative to the fingers before proceeding to the bin.
The white bottle follows the hand. Lift and carry it left toward the bin with closure maintained, gradually easing the overhead wrist pitch.
Carry the retained white bottle toward the middle of the bin, preserving height and keeping the left grasp closed.
Shift the retained white bottle farther inside the bin perimeter, then open and hold to release it.
Let the third bottle fall clear. Begin the right-hand approach for the remaining yellow bottle using small initial steps, while retracting the left hand within its own workspace.
Raise and orient the right hand for an overhead yellow-bottle grasp. Bring the left hand toward a separate central receiving position, keeping the arms on their own sides.
Continue the right overhead approach, rotating across the yellow bottle axis. Position the open left hand for a later handover without crossing the arms.
Finish the right overhead orientation and lower toward the yellow bottle body; hold the left hand open at a separate receiving location.
Correct the right pinch center from the wrist view, descend slightly to the bottle body and close without moving the receiving hand.
Finish the right-hand closure and lift vertically to verify the yellow bottle is retained before the handover.
Yellow bottle follows the right hand. Lift and begin turning it upright for handover; move the open left hand slightly back for rotation clearance.
Continue turning the retained bottle upright in the right workspace. Raise the open left receiver to a different height so it can grasp above the donor fingers.
Finish presenting the bottle upright while advancing the open left hand toward its upper body. Keep the donor closed and the receiver higher to avoid finger interference.
Replan after the right-arm continuity stop with much smaller rotation increments. Bring the left fingers around the upper bottle while preserving donor retention.
Adjust the left pinch laterally around the upper bottle, then close the receiver while the right donor remains closed and stationary.
Keep the left receiver closed, open the right donor, then withdraw the right hand slightly. Verify that the bottle remains with the left hand.
The bottle remains supported by the left receiver after donor opening. Carry it left toward the bin, while retracting the open right hand within its workspace.
Yellow bottle is retained by the left hand. Carry toward the bin while turning the wrist inward; return the open right arm gradually toward its origin.
Bring the last bottle fully over the bin while keeping it closed. Complete most of the right arm's return, with small orientation corrections.
Open the left hand over the bin and wait for the yellow bottle to fall clear. Settle the right arm at its origin before returning the left.
The yellow bottle has fallen clear and the table is empty. Return the open left hand toward origin along a continuous elbow-up path; right hand remains at origin.
